newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - T-bond back in neutral as uptick fizzles.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - T-bond back in neutral as uptick fizzles.

text.p: June T-bond futures on the CBOT, will slip back into neutral on Friday, having failed to capitalise on a break of key resistance at 107-28 in the previous session, analysts said.
Prices would likely be confined to Thursday's 107-14 to 108-07 range. A close over 108-00 would negate the downward tug.
"It's looking pretty neutral," said Charles Diebel, senior fixed income analyst at Technical Data in London. "We're back off the lows but it doesn't look like it will extend higher."
T-bonds were quoted at 107-27 at 0926 GMT, unchanged from the pit settlement in Chicago on Thursday.
The market broke above the April range high at 107-28 on Thursday but failed to extend the move, drifting down to a close of 107-27.
Richard Adcock, manager of technical research at HSBC Markets here, also noted Thursday's failure to hold gains above 108-00.

"The worry is that we're seeing an unwinding of oversold levels just with the market moving sideways," he said, adding there was a danger Treasuries may turn lower after these oversold positions were totally unwound. To abort that threat, the market must close above 108-00 fairly soon, he said.
Diebel said if the market did push through the top of Thursday's range it would target the March 27 high of 108-23.
Adcock saw psychological resistance at the big figure of 109-00.
For support, T-bonds would find a buffer around Thursday's 107-14 low and then at the 106-17 low on Wednesday, Diebel said.
Adcock also saw support at 107-15 -- the mid-point of the current sideways trading area.
September Eurodollars were quoted at 93.760, up 0.015 in automated trade.
